canonical.title: Which React router to adopt in 2026: a decision framework for a client-rendered admin SPA

siblings.title: The 2026 React Router Landscape: TanStack Router vs React Router vs Wouter vs Next.js
siblings.summary: For a client-rendered React 19 admin SPA, TanStack Router is the sharpest fit and React Router the safest default; Wouter is for simple apps and Next.js App Router is the wrong grain.

siblings.title: Type-Safe Routing & Typed Search-Param State in React (2026)
siblings.summary: TanStack Router is the only router with typed, schema-validated search-param state end to end — the decisive edge for a filter-heavy admin console, at the cost of advanced-type complexity.

siblings.title: Router-driven data loading in React (2026): who owns the cache?
siblings.summary: For a CSR-only admin SPA on a REST/OpenAPI backend, let a query library own the cache and keep the router thin — framework loaders only pay off with SSR.

siblings.title: Library-mode router vs meta-framework (and RSC) for a React 19 admin SPA in 2026
siblings.summary: For an auth-gated internal admin SPA, a standalone router on Vite is still a first-class 2026 choice; RSC and meta-frameworks solve problems this app doesn't have.

siblings.title: Migration Effort & Lock-In: Choosing a React Router in 2026
siblings.summary: Already on React Router? Staying is near-drop-in. Greenfield SPA? The lock-in and churn math tilts toward TanStack Router.

sources.title: TanStack Router
sources.claim: @tanstack/react-router has over 12.7M weekly npm downloads; a May 2026 npm supply-chain attack briefly compromised 42 @tanstack/* packages for ~20 minutes.

sources.title: React Router — Modes
sources.claim: React Router has three additive modes; framework mode wraps data mode with a Vite plugin for type-safe routing and flexible rendering.

sources.title: TanStack Router — Comparison
sources.claim: TanStack Router offers full type-safe path and search params in SPA mode; React Router partial; Next.js file-based only.

sources.title: React Router — Type Safety
sources.claim: React Router generates per-route .d.ts via typegen, available only in framework mode — not data or declarative mode.

sources.title: TanStack Router — Type Safety
sources.claim: End-to-end type safety across route params, search params, loaders, context and Link at compile time, SSR or not.

sources.title: Search Params Are State
sources.claim: Search params are first-class serializable, shareable state that must be schema-validated at the route.

sources.title: TanStack Router vs React Router v7 (2026)
sources.claim: React Router v7 SPA mode needs manual casts like useLoaderData() as Post and untyped URLSearchParams.

sources.title: TanStack Router and Query — TkDodo
sources.claim: With TanStack Query, disable the router's cache so one player owns caching; loaders become fire-and-forget priming.

sources.title: React Router discussion #14037
sources.claim: For CSR-only apps TanStack Query alone works without framework mode; running both loaders and Query in parallel is an anti-pattern.

sources.title: React Server Components — Growin
sources.claim: RSC is an architectural boundary not an optimization; interactive dashboards become mostly client-bound, collapsing the server-first advantage.

sources.title: Next.js vs React + Vite
sources.claim: The React team points SPA projects at Vite; React + Vite wins for auth-gated pages where a brief loading state is fine.

sources.title: Migrate from React Router
sources.claim: Migrating a standard small SPA from React Router to TanStack Router takes ~2-4 hours; the two can coexist during transition.

sources.title: React Router discussion #15015
sources.claim: The v6-to-v7 codemod automated ~85-90% of migration changes across 461 real-world files with zero false positives.

sources.title: TanStack Router — Decisions on DX
sources.claim: Type safety relies on very advanced and complex TypeScript inference with a real learning curve.

sources.title: React Router v8
sources.claim: React Router v8 shipped June 2026, the 'most boring' major yet; breaking changes are pre-adoptable in v7 behind future flags.

sources.title: Wouter
sources.claim: A minimalist ~2.2KB hooks-based router for React and Preact with familiar Route/Link/Switch components.

sources.title: Next.js
sources.claim: The React Framework; server-first, dominant for full-stack apps, the wrong grain for a client-rendered admin console.

sources.title: @rtk-query/codegen-openapi
sources.claim: RTK Query ships an official OpenAPI code generator producing fully-typed endpoints from a spec.
